question: How should a dropout predictor be audited before use?
data: UCI 697: 4,424 historical student records; 20 retained predictors.
method: Exclude post-enrollment and audit-only fields; train/test evaluation, calibration, subgroup support checks and threshold sensitivity.
formula: Brier = mean((p-y)^2); selection gap = max(group rates)-min(group rates).
interpretation: No recorded dropout includes enrolled and graduated cases; it is not synonymous with success. Group rates need adequate positive and negative support. An unevaluable group must not be represented as having zero disparity.
status: RECORDED EXTERNAL-DATA STUDY | full experiment not rerun in this review
table_title: Selected recorded values (units and context shown)
evidence_note: Selected committed results; source values were not independently retrained in this review.
finding: The primary holdout reports ROC-AUC 0.8316 and Brier score 0.1447. Gender diagnostics can be calculated, while international, intersectional, and special-needs audits remain unevaluable under the support rules. Repeated splits and bootstrap checks describe uncertainty, but incomplete governance evidence and the historical dataset prevent a deployment or fairness certification.
